All zero-margin bases originally contributed their full masses, and the own interior ball loses one half of its volume. This contradicts attainment even if every sampled base lies in the old plane.

A nonvertical cap through an own-fiber interior point has a positive proper own section. Apply the two-sided normal and threshold variation to the positive-volume fibers alone. Proper traces have the signed derivative, strictly full and empty traces are locally constant, and all other supporting traces, on either side, have zero (d−1)-measure. Null-volume fibers make zero contribution to every cap and its variation even if an unmeasured section has positive (d−1)-measure. At a fixed anchor Y the threshold perturbation is exactly the perturbing normal applied to Y. The standalone section formula requires neither an ambient-interior depth region nor a regular projected base.

The strict-contact lemma applies with a proper own section and directional differentiability for every signed ambient perturbation through Y. It excludes every different point of at least that depth from the closed attaining cap, including a point on the old boundary. Strictly convex positive fibers have singleton supporting faces, which are null in dimension d−1 for d≥2. The proof itself uses the stated measure condition, so flat lower-dimensional support faces are allowed.

A sampled intermediate point has at least the lesser endpoint depth by the affine-margin test. If equality held, its actual minimizing cap contains at least one endpoint of depth at least its own, violating strict contact. The reasoning is independent of whether the endpoint bases coincide. Same-parity maximizing points have a sampled midpoint in C, which would have strictly larger depth. The number of ambient parity classes is exactly 2^n, and two marks at the same base lie in one class.

For any integer p′ in the finite hull, lift a finite convex combination using the unique maximizing mark at each participating base. Convexity and integrality put the lift in S, and each containing halfspace contains at least one participating mark, hence the lift is maximizing. If the representation uses a distinct base with positive weight, its mark has strictly negative margin at any attaining cap through the lift, while all other margins are nonpositive. Their weighted average cannot be zero. This proves extremality and the lattice census even in a lower-dimensional hull.

The global maximizing mark maximizes on its positive own fiber. A positive circuit of actual nonvertical minimizing through-caps exists. For every different maximizing mark, each margin is strictly negative, so every positive weighted sum remains strictly negative there. The continuous terms cancel exactly by circuit balance, leaving the base functional with a strictly smaller value at all other bases. When the hull has at least two bases this functional is nonzero, and with one base any nonzero base functional uniquely maximizes there.

overlap.comparison: Sections 2–3 give the same single-cap regular contact consequence from null nonproper traces and positive coarea. The accepted projected contact/facet results assume extra conditions on a projected level, whereas this proposition uses an own-fiber interior ball at each positive-depth mark to obtain strict sampled interpolation and the global maximizing-base hull.

The abstract proper-cap contact lemma is the exact local implication used here. Its statement assumes the differentiability of one specified cap, whereas the new theorem verifies that premise for every attaining through-cap at a positive-depth sample under a structural fiber hypothesis and gives the interpolation, parity and circuit hull conclusions.

Its fixed-face consequence gives lattice completeness, extremality and a parity bound for the maximizing bases of the positive-buffer fixed-face cover (whose premise 09a0ec46efc18691 requires epsilon>0). That conclusion does not directly specialize to all ordinary raw maximizing marks at epsilon=0 and does not give their strict interpolation or the raw circuit exposing functional.

Provides the actual positive circuit at own-fiber maximizing marks for compatible families. The strict sign on every distinct global mark and the exposed-base conclusion are not implied by balance alone without the null-section contact argument.
